Subject: Post-call recap + DPA / privacy questions (MedSys POC)

Hi Amit / Priya —

Thanks for the time on today’s discovery call. Quick recap and the items we promised to follow up on related to privacy/data handling for the POC: 

1) High-level roles: you asked whether Redwood is a Controller or Processor for this integration.
2) Subprocessors: you asked for our current subprocessors list and notification cadence for changes.
3) Breach notice: you requested target timelines for incident notification and an outline of how we communicate confirmed vs suspected incidents.
4) Data residency & retention: PII retention windows and whether we can keep data in a single region (us-east-1) for the POC.
5) Logging & access controls: what logs we keep, how long, and what redaction/tokenization options are available.

Attached: Redwood_DPA_v2.1.pdf (clean copy), SOC2-report-summary.pdf. I’ve also added a quick mapping spreadsheet (medsys-mapping.xlsx) with the POC data flows you sketched.

Next steps I propose: 
- Legal-to-legal call (30 min) to walk DPA language; please share your availability next week.
- Confirm whether MedSys will sign Redwood as Processor (typical) or request an alternate arrangement.
- If residency requirement is confirmed (e.g., us-east-1), we’ll validate runtime placement and provide proof of residency controls.

If you want, I can prepare a short pre-call checklist for your legal/security team (items they usually ask for).

Thanks — looking forward to the next steps.

Best,
Priyom Das
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Post-call recap + DPA / privacy questions (MedSys POC)

Thanks for the recap, Priyom — useful summary. A few clarifications before we schedule legal: 

- Controller/Processor: MedSys will be Controller for PII collected for clinical workflows. We expect Redwood to operate as Processor. Please confirm DPA language aligns with that model and note any exceptions (e.g., cases where Redwood acts as a controller for aggregated telemetry).

- Subprocessors: we need a current list and a commitment to notify and allow reasonable review (14 days) before any new subprocessor onboarding. Will Redwood accept that notice period?

- Breach notice: our policy requires notification of confirmed breaches within 24 hours to our security team, and a 72-hour update cadence until containment. Can you confirm Redwood’s operational SLA?

- Retention & deletion: PII retention must be configurable per POC dataset (our default ask: 30 days for raw PII, 365 days for de-identified logs). How do you support configurable retention windows, and can you confirm secure deletion practice?

- Residency: For the POC we need all processing to remain in us-east-1. We may expand to EU later for production.

If you can get Laura and Neha’s short answers on the above, we can lock in a time for a brief legal/security call.

Best,
Amit Shah
Director, Engineering (Security)
MedSys, Inc.

Hi Amit / Priyom —

Thanks — below are short answers and proposed language we can use in the DPA. Happy to take these live on a legal-to-legal call and walk through examples.

1) Controller vs Processor
- Default: Redwood acts as Processor of PII/data you send for inference and storage for the POC. Redlined clause we propose: "Redwood Inference shall process Customer Personal Data only on documented instructions from Customer and shall not determine purposes and means of processing except for processing strictly necessary for service delivery and performance optimization."
- Exception: Aggregated telemetry (service health metrics, anonymized usage) is used by Redwood for product improvements; we do not tie telemetry back to identifiable patient records.

2) Subprocessors + notice period
- We will provide the current subprocessors list in advance of the call (include cloud provider, monitoring, and analytics vendors). Redwood’s standard commitment: 30 days notice for new subprocessors. For MedSys POC we can accept a 14-day review window as a one-off for the POC with documented exceptions.

3) Breach notification cadence
- Operational practice: initial confirmed-incident notification within 24 hours (business hours), with follow-up updates at 72 hours and then daily until containment. For suspected incidents, we notify within 48 hours and follow the same update cadence. We can include this timeline in the DPA.

4) Retention & deletion
- Redwood supports configurable retention per dataset. Options we can enforce at the tenant level: immediate ephemeral (no persistent storage), 30 days, 90 days, 365 days. Secure deletion: cryptographic key revocation and certified deletion of object storage per process. We will document retention configuration in the POC runbook.

5) Residency & logging controls
- Residency: we can pin processing to a single cloud region (us-east-1) for the POC. We will provide proofs: VPC subnet mappings and runtime placement logs.
- Logging: request-level logs are retained per agreed retention window; we provide token redaction and can enable PII scrubbing at ingestion. Access to logs is role-based and audited.

Attachments: I’ll attach a redline of Redwood_DPA_v2.1.pdf with the proposed language (Redwood_DPA_v2.1_redline.pdf) and SOC2 artifact link.

Next steps:
- Laura (Redwood) + legal at MedSys — propose 30-min call. Priyom: please suggest 3 windows next week; I’ll include the redline in calendar invite.
- Neha: can you prepare the short pre-call checklist and confirm we can export residency proof (VPC + runtime logs) before the call?

Regards,
Laura Bennett
Head of Legal
Redwood Inference
